design: mult (scale stream s5 run, track router, schema 6; measured with feat/rtl2gds-extract2 merged with feat/rtl2gds-scale b363d0f)

scope.magic_timing: per-net Magic totals back-annotated onto native RC trees

scope.coupling_reason: listed in both nets so totals and SPEF consumers see the same capacitance; the timing engine grounds coupling at factor 1
scope.via_capacitance: landing pads extracted (pad metal outside the wires is a capacitance-only piece at the via node); cut capacitance unmodeled
scope.wire_ends: half-width end extensions (DEF default) extracted as capacitance-only pieces at the run end node
scope.metal_union: wire bodies and pieces (end extensions, via pads, patches) tile the routed metal without overlap; sides inside or touching same-net metal (including the net's own pins) are not exposed
scope.passive_conductors: pins, obstructions and supply metal that a routed conductor crosses count their own cross-section toward it (the second cut of a crossing); their ground and lateral sides are counted from the routed side
scope.crossings: a conductor is a calibration plate where its layer covers the strip and reaches one strip width beyond both edges; a plate below shields the substrate; both wires of a crossing count their own cross-section
scope.parallel_overlap: narrower, offset or barely wider metal on other layers is not a plate: the covered face of the upper conductor couples by the profile's overlap-area capacitance (counted once) and loses its face-to-substrate area capacitance; fringe of such overlaps unmodeled
scope.cell_internal_metal: pins and obstructions are neighbours, plates and overlap partners; their own metal is not extracted
scope.routing_patches: extracted: each piece not covered by same-net metal adds ground and coupling on all four edges at the RC node of the same-net conductor it overlaps (no new node or resistor)

min.method: per net: merged stored wires Rs*L/W plus vias, against the SPEF resistors; nets whose record graph has a loop are left out (the extractor opens the loop)

nom.method: per net: merged stored wires Rs*L/W plus vias, against the SPEF resistors; nets whose record graph has a loop are left out (the extractor opens the loop)

determinism.compared: per-net c_pf, coupling_pf, r_ohm at nom (two runs)

min.meaning: passed: grounding a sub-threshold coupling keeps the design total (it is grounded in one net, not both)

nom.meaning: passed: grounding a sub-threshold coupling keeps the design total (it is grounded in one net, not both)

max.meaning: passed: grounding a sub-threshold coupling keeps the design total (it is grounded in one net, not both)

openrcx_obs_blind.meaning: passed: OpenRCX gives identical per-net C without the cell OBS, i.e. it does not extract cell obstructions (native and Magic do)

openrcx_pin_blind.meaning: passed: no net loses more than the bound when every signal pin shrinks to a 10 nm square, i.e. OpenRCX does not count cell pin metal as a coupling or ground partner of any net (native and Magic do). Increases (and R changes) come from a net's own wire metal over its own pin, which OpenRCX merges into the pin while the pin is full size
